question.text: What additional measures must a Regulated Entity undertake when a customer is determined to be a Politically Exposed Person (PEP)?

answer.text: Collect adequate information about source of wealth and income (including family members, close relatives and beneficial owners); obtain Senior Management approval before opening or continuing the account; and increase the degree and nature of ongoing monitoring of the business relationship
Collect information about source of wealth and income of family members and close relatives
Obtain Senior Management approval before opening an account
Increase the degree and nature of ongoing monitoring of the business relationship

explanation.text: The Logic: For PEPs, the IFSCA Guidelines require additional measures including: (i) collecting adequate information about source of wealth and income of the customer, family members, beneficial owners and close relatives; (ii) obtaining Senior Management approval before opening the account, and again to continue an existing relationship if the customer subsequently becomes a PEP; and (iii) increasing the degree and nature of ongoing monitoring of the business relationship. The Trap: Each single-measure distractor is correct on its own, but the PEP regime requires all of these measures together. PEP measures also extend beyond the customer to family members, close associates and beneficial owners — not just the named PEP. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone option that explicitly lists source-of-wealth/income information, Senior Management approval, and increased ongoing monitoring, and removed the cross-exam/pro-tip lines that were not source-grounded.
